div.head: Hn 71.1
div.ab: Si quis ueneno uel sortilegio uel inuultuacione seu maleficio aliquo faciat homicidium, siue illi paratum sit siue alii, nichil refert, quin factum mortiferum et nullo modo redimendum sit.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 590 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: bewitchment by injuring a sculpted image

Über Zauber (s. d. Gl 6a; busslos 5C) im Strafrecht s. Pol Mai II 551.—Ducange belegt invultuare ‘Abbild machen’, vultuare ‘durch Magie töten’, invultuor, vultuarius ‘Magier’. Johanna, Gemahlin Philipps IV, invultatione decesserat; Eleonore Cobham soll 1441 Heinrich dem VI. durch Schmelzen seines Wachsbildes nach dem Leben getrachtet haben. (An bezauberndes Anschauen oder bösen Blick ist nicht zu denken.) Über defixio, punctura durch Nadelstechen bei Agsa. vgl. Toller s. v. staca, die Pönitentialien Ps. Egb. IV 18 = Mod. impon. poen. 38; H. S. Cuming Pinlore and the waxen image im Journ. Brit. archl. assoc. 1899, 161.—siue{18} fehlt Rs

On magic (see that word in Gl 6a; busslos 5C) in criminal law see Pol Mai II 551.—Ducange attests invultuare ‘to make an image’, vultuare ‘to kill by magic’, invultuor, vultuarius ‘magician’. Joan, wife of Philip IV, invultatione decesserat; in 1441 Eleanor Cobham is said to have sought the life of Henry VI by melting his wax image. (Bewitching looks or the evil eye are not to be thought of.) On defixio, punctura by pricking with needles among the Anglo-Saxons cf. Toller s. v. staca, the penitentials Ps. Egb. IV 18 = Mod. impon. poen. 38; H. S. Cuming Pinlore and the waxen image in Journ. Brit. archl. assoc. 1899, 161.—siue{18} missing Rs

div.ab: If anyone commits homicide by poison or by sorcery or by image-magic or by any witchcraft, whether it was prepared for him or for another, it makes no difference: the deed is deadly and can in no way be redeemed.
